perustuslaki.title: Suomen perustuslaki (731/1999)
perustuslaki.note: The Constitution of Finland: s.24 (a unicameral Eduskunta of 200 members elected for four years), s.53 (consultative referendums), s.54 (the President elected directly for six years), s.120 (Åland's autonomy), and s.121 (municipal self-government and Sámi cultural self-government).

vaalilaki.title: Vaalilaki (714/1998)
vaalilaki.note: The Election Act, consolidated: s.5 (13 constituencies for the Eduskunta), s.6 (199 proportional seats plus one for Åland), s.7 (the whole country one constituency for the President and the European Parliament; the wellbeing services county and the municipality the constituency in county and municipal elections), s.107 (parliamentary election day), s.112-115 (party member ballots), s.127 (presidential election day), s.144 (municipal election day), and s.160 (European Parliament election day).

kuntalaki.title: Kuntalaki (410/2015)
kuntalaki.note: The Local Government Act: s.15 (councillors elected in municipal elections for a four-year term from 1 June of the election year), s.16 (the number of councillors), s.24-25 (consultative municipal referendums and referendum initiatives), and s.18 (the council's chair), and s.44 (a mayor chosen by the council).

hyvinvointialuelaki.title: Laki hyvinvointialueesta (611/2021)
hyvinvointialuelaki.note: The Act on Wellbeing Services Counties: each county has a county council (aluevaltuusto) whose members are elected in the county elections.

saamelaiskarajalaki.title: Laki saamelaiskäräjistä (974/1995)
saamelaiskarajalaki.note: The Act on the Sámi Parliament, in force 1 January 1996: 21 members and four deputies elected for four years from 1 December of the election year; the whole country is one constituency; elections every fourth year, by post and in the Sámi homeland also on election day.

kainuulaki.title: Laki Kainuun hallintokokeilusta (343/2003)
kainuulaki.note: The Kainuu regional self-government experiment, repealed from 31 December 2012: a directly elected regional council (maakuntavaltuusto) for the Kainuu region.

classes.name: Eduskuntavaalit
classes.finest_note: Votes by voting district (äänestysalue) in the results service from 2011 and in StatFin tables for recent elections; by municipality in StatFin from 1983; earlier volumes by municipality in the Official Statistics of Finland series.
classes.note: 200 members for four years (Constitution s.24): 199 by D'Hondt among open lists in 12 constituencies (13 counted with Åland) and one in Åland by plurality (Election Act s.6). Fifteen constituencies until 2011; 13 from 2015. Elections from 1907, under the Grand Duchy, belong to the same body. There are no by-elections: a vacancy goes to the next candidate of the list (Election Act s.92), and only an Åland vacancy with no deputy forces a new poll there.

cadence.locator: https://www.finlex.fi/fi/lainsaadanto/1998/714 (s.107: "Eduskuntavaalien vaalipäivä on huhtikuun kolmas sunnuntai." Early elections 50 to 75 days after the President's order)

cadence.vacancy_rule: The next candidate of the same list by comparative figure takes the seat (Election Act s.92); a new poll only in Åland when no deputy remains.

classes.name: Presidentinvaali
classes.note: Elected directly for six years, at most two consecutive terms; a candidate with more than half the votes wins, otherwise the top two meet in a second round (Constitution s.54). First round on the fourth Sunday of January, second round two weeks later (Election Act s.127). The 1988 direct vote ran beside an electors' vote (class president_electors).

cadence.locator: https://www.finlex.fi/fi/lainsaadanto/1998/714 (s.127: "Presidentinvaalin ensimmäisen vaalin vaalipäivä on tammikuun neljäs sunnuntai kuudentena vuotena sen vuoden jälkeen, jona tasavallan presidentti viimeksi ryhtyi toimeensa.")
cadence.runoff_rule: The two leading candidates meet in a second round on the second Sunday after the first (Constitution s.54; Election Act s.127).
cadence.administered_by: Ministry of Justice; the Helsinki constituency electoral committee draws up the candidate list

classes.name: Valitsijamiesvaalit
classes.note: From 1919 to 1987 the President was chosen by 300 electors (301 in 1982 and 1988) elected by popular vote by constituency; the 1937 electors also chose in 1940 and 1943, and Parliament or special Acts chose in 1919, 1944, and 1946. In 1988 the electors were elected at the same poll as the direct vote and chose the President because no candidate won a majority. The popular vote for electors is the contest held; the electors' own ballot is not.

classes.name: Europarlamenttivaalit
classes.note: The whole country is one constituency (Election Act s.7); seats go to open lists by D'Hondt. The first election, of 1996, was held apart from the EU-wide cycle; since 1999 on the Sunday in the Council's June window (s.160).

classes.name: Neuvoa-antavat kansanäänestykset
classes.note: Every national referendum is consultative and needs its own Act setting the date and the alternatives (Constitution s.53). Two have been held: on prohibition, 29 and 30 December 1931 (Act 340/31), and on joining the European Union, 16 October 1994. Åland voted on EU membership again on 20 November 1994 under its own law (AX census).

cadence.locator: https://www.finlex.fi/fi/lainsaadanto/1999/731 (s.53: "Neuvoa-antavan kansanäänestyksen järjestämisestä päätetään lailla, jossa on säädettävä äänestyksen ajankohdasta ja äänestäjille esitettävistä vaihtoehdoista.")

classes.name: Kuntavaalit
classes.finest_note: Each municipality is one constituency; votes by voting district in the results service from 2012, by municipality in StatFin from 1976.
classes.note: Each mainland municipality's council is elected for four years from 1 June of the election year (Local Government Act s.15) by D'Hondt among open lists, the municipality being one constituency (Election Act s.7). Universal-suffrage municipal elections go back to the municipal Acts of 1917; StatFin's series starts in 1976, and earlier elections are not yet listed here. Åland's 16 municipalities elect under Åland law (AX census). Held in October until 2012, then in April (2021 moved to June).

cadence.locator: https://www.finlex.fi/fi/lainsaadanto/1998/714 (s.144: "Kuntavaalien vaalipäivä on huhtikuun kolmas sunnuntai." "Kuntavaalit toimitetaan samanaikaisesti aluevaalien kanssa.")
cadence.vacancy_rule: The next candidate of the same list becomes councillor; councillors' deputies come from the list (Local Government Act s.17).

classes.name: Saamelaiskäräjien vaalit
classes.note: 21 members and four deputies elected for four years from 1 December of the election year by people entered in the Sámi electoral roll, the whole country one constituency, in a six-week postal vote from the Monday of the last full week of August and on election day in the Sámi homeland (Act 974/1995). The Sámi Delegation (saamelaisvaltuuskunta, 1973-1995) that preceded it was also elected and is not yet listed.

cadence.locator: https://www.finlex.fi/fi/lainsaadanto/1995/974 ("Saamelaiskäräjien vaalit toimitetaan joka neljäs vuosi"; "Saamelaiskäräjien vaalit toimitetaan elokuun viimeisen täyden viikon maanantaista alkavan kuuden viikon aikana.")

classes.name: Kunnalliset kansanäänestykset
classes.note: A council may put any municipal matter to a consultative referendum of the whole municipality or of some voting districts (Local Government Act s.24); 4 percent of residents aged 15 or more may initiate one (s.25). The procedure is Act 656/1990, which also covers wellbeing services counties. Most were held on municipal mergers; the Ministry of Justice keeps the list.

classes.name: Säätyvaltiopäivät
classes.disposition_reason: The Diet of the Grand Duchy sat by estate: nobles by birth, and clergy, burghers, and peasants chosen by their own corporations and electors under property and status rules; these were not public elections, and no official vote counts were compiled. The Parliament Act of 1906 replaced it with the unicameral Eduskunta (class eduskunta).

classes.name: Seurakuntavaalit
classes.disposition_reason: Parish councils are elected by church members under the Church Act and the church's own election rules, run and published by the churches, not by the state election authority.

classes.name: Puolueiden jäsenäänestykset
classes.disposition_reason: Where more people seek a party's nomination than it may field, the party holds a member ballot under its own rules (Election Act ss.112-115); the party, not the state, runs and records it.

classes.name: Valtuuston ja pormestarin valinta
classes.name_en: Council chairs and mayors chosen by councils
classes.disposition_reason: The council elects its chair (Local Government Act s.18) and, where it chooses mayoral government, the mayor (s.44); these are councillors' votes recorded in minutes, not public elections.
